newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stock market ends week higher, led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stock market ends week higher, led by banks.

text.p: Shares on Saudi Arabia's stock market ended last week higher in firm trade, helped by high turnover on banking sector shares, the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) said.
The all-share index closed 0.9 percent higher to a 162.35 point close on Wednesday from 160.92 points the previous Thursday.
BFA put trading value at 721 million riyals ($192 million), up by about 20 percent from a week earlier.
Of the 58 shares traded, 36 rose, 10 fell and 12 were unchanged.
BFA said bank shares accounted for 35 percent of trading value, followed by cement shares at 25 percent. Riyadh Bank was the most actively traded share in the week.
Thimar was the week's star performer, closing 18.2 percent higher at 78 riyals from 66 riyals the previous week. Al-Aziza Panda was among major gainers, closing at 125 riyals from 118 riyals.
Beshah Agriculture ended the week lower at 30 rials from 35 riyals and SAIC lost six riyals to 60 riyals.
